front.title: Agent Discovery Protocol (ADP) v1.1 — Well-Known Metadata and Interaction Layer

abstract.t: This document defines the Agent Discovery Protocol (ADP) v1.1, a
layered protocol for discovering, verifying, and interacting with AI
Agents on the Internet. ADP delegates DNS discovery to DNS-AID (SVCB
records) and defines a Well-Known JSON metadata format, an
Ed25519-based identity model, and the Agent Gateway Protocol (AGP)
for real-time WebSocket messaging. The protocol is designed to be
decentralized, standards-based, and incremental — clients escalate
from DNS to HTTP to WebSocket only as needed.

section.title: Background
section.t: AI Agents are evolving from chatbot plugins into autonomous,
internet-native entities. Each platform (OpenAI, Dify, Coze)
provides its own directory and identity system, but there is no
universal discovery mechanism: an Agent on one platform cannot
natively discover an Agent on another without a bridging registry.
The Web solved an analogous problem decades ago: any resource can be
discovered through a combination of DNS names, well-known ports, and
HTML interlinking. ADP applies the same principle to Agents, adding
what the Web assumes but Agents require: structured capability
descriptions, cryptographic identity binding, and real-time
communication primitives.

section.title: Relationship to DNS-AID
section.t: DNS-AID defines the DNS discovery
layer for Agents using SVCB records . It registers the

ul.li: bap: Bulk Agent Protocol identifier (e.g., a2a, mcp).
cap: URI or URN of the Agent's capability descriptor.
cap-sha256: SHA-256 digest of the capability descriptor.
well-known: Path relative to /.well-known/ for the Agent's metadata

section.t: document.
ADP v1.1 adopts DNS-AID as its normative DNS discovery mechanism. The
ADP Well-Known JSON schema () serves as the content format
pointed to by the well-known SvcParamKey.
If DNS-AID is unavailable (the DNS resolver does not support SVCB, or
the authoritative server has not published SVCB records), ADP provides
a fallback path using TXT and SRV records as
documented in .

section.title: Design Goals

ul.li: *Decentralized*: No central registry; domain ownership is the root

section.t: of identity.

ul.li: *Layered and incremental*: SVCB answers connectivity in one round

section.t: trip; Well-Known provides full metadata; WebSocket enables
real-time chat. Do not escalate to a heavier layer when a lighter
one suffices.

ul.li: *Standards-based*: Built on SVCB , TLSA ,

section.t: DNSSEC , Well-Known URIs , WebSocket
, and Ed25519 .

ul.li: *Aligned with IETF work*: DNS layer defers to DNS-AID

section.t: . ADP focuses on what happens
after discovery.

ul.li: *Human-and-machine readable*: The root URL serves both a browser

section.t: user and an automated client via JSON-LD embedding.

ul.li: *Secure by default*: DNS-AID + TLSA/DANE anchors the TLS endpoint;

section.t: Ed25519 signatures authenticate messages end-to-end.

section.title: Terminology

dl.dd: An autonomous or semi-autonomous software entity identified by a

section.t: domain name, capable of being discovered through DNS-AID + ADP and
interacting via standard Web protocols.

dl.dd: A fully qualified domain name (FQDN) that serves as the canonical

section.t: identifier for an Agent. The Agent URI scheme is
agent:{domain}.

dl.dd: Software that performs discovery to locate and verify an Agent's

section.t: identity, capabilities, and endpoints.

dl.dd: The SHA-256 hash of an Ed25519 public key, encoded in base64url

section.t: without padding and prefixed with ed25519:.

dl.dd: The WebSocket-based messaging protocol defined in , used

section.t: for inter-agent communication after discovery.

dl.dd: The DNS-based Agent Identity and Discovery mechanism defined in

section.t: , which serves as ADP's
normative Layer 1.

section.title: Protocol Overview
section.t: The Agent Discovery Protocol defines a three-layer discovery and
Layer 1 — DNS Discovery (delegated to DNS-AID): A single SVCB
query at the Agent's domain name returns the target, port, IP
hints, ALPN protocol list, Agent protocol identifier (bap),
capability descriptor URI (cap), its SHA-256 digest (cap-sha256),
and the Well-Known URI path (well-known). TLSA records enable
DANE-based TLS endpoint authentication. TXT+SRV records serve
as fallback.
Layer 2 — Well-Known Metadata (this document): A GET request
to the Well-Known URI (default /.well-known/agent.json) returns
a JSON document containing the Agent's identity, capabilities,
relationships, security policies, and endpoint map.
Layer 3 — Interaction Endpoints (this document): An HTML
landing page at the domain root provides human-readable discovery
with embedded JSON-LD structured data. WebSocket endpoints using
the Agent Gateway Protocol (AGP) enable real-time inter-agent
communication with Ed25519 signature authentication.
*Core principle*: If SVCB answers your question, do not issue an HTTP
request. If Well-Known suffices, do not open a WebSocket.

section.title: Layer 1: DNS Discovery (DNS-AID)
section.t: ADP v1.1 delegates its DNS discovery layer to DNS-AID
. This section summarizes the
integration points; the normative specification resides in that
document.

section.title: SVCB Record (RECOMMENDED)
section.t: An ADP-compliant Agent SHOULD publish a SVCB record at its domain
name.

figure.artwork: alice.example.com. 3600 IN SVCB 1 . ( alpn="a2a,h2,h3" port=443 ipv4hint=192.0.2.1 ipv6hint=2001:db8::1 bap=a2a well-known=agent.json cap=https://alice.example.com/capabilities/a2a.json cap-sha256=<sha256-digest> )

section.title: SvcParamKey Usage in ADP

dl.dd: The application-layer protocol negotiation IDs . ADP

section.t: Agents SHOULD include the relevant Agent protocol identifier
(e.g., a2a) alongside standard HTTP protocol IDs (h2, h3).

dl.dd: Bulk Agent Protocol identifier. Separated from alpn so that

section.t: policy engines can match on Agent-level protocol without parsing
transport protocol negotiation. ADP v1.1 defines the protocol
identifier a2a for the AGP messaging protocol ().

dl.dd: Path relative to the Well-Known URI namespace. Discovery

section.t: Clients MUST resolve this against
https://{target}/.well-known/{well-known}. If absent, the
default path /.well-known/agent.json is used.

dl.dd: URI or URN identifying the Agent's capability descriptor. ADP

section.t: Agents SHOULD publish this as a URL to their capability document.

dl.dd: SHA-256 digest of the capability descriptor at the time of DNS

section.t: publishing. Allows a Discovery Client to verify that the
capability document has not changed without re-fetching.

section.title: Hosted Agents (TargetName)
section.t: When an Agent is hosted by a third-party provider, the SVCB
TargetName field points to the provider's domain.

figure.artwork: alice.example.com. 3600 IN SVCB 1 provider.example.com. ( alpn="a2a,h2" port=443 bap=a2a well-known=agent.json )

section.title: Organization Index (AliasMode)
section.t: Organizations MAY publish an index of their Agents using AliasMode.

figure.artwork: _agents.example.com. 3600 IN SVCB 0 alice.example.com. _agents.example.com. 3600 IN SVCB 0 bob.example.com.

section.title: TLSA Record (RECOMMENDED with DNSSEC)
section.t: ADP Agents SHOULD publish a TLSA record to enable DANE-based TLS
endpoint authentication.

ul.li: TLSA records are only valid when the DNS zone is DNSSEC-signed

section.t: , to prevent downgrade attacks.

ul.li: The RECOMMENDED usage is DANE-EE (3), selector SPKI (1), matching

section.t: type SHA-256 (1).

ul.li: A Discovery Client that receives both a valid TLSA record and a

section.t: certificate that does not match MUST terminate the connection.

section.title: DNSSEC
section.t: All DNS records used for Agent discovery SHOULD be DNSSEC-signed.
TLSA records MUST be DNSSEC-signed to be trusted.

section.title: Fallback Discovery: TXT + SRV
section.t: When the DNS resolver or authoritative server does not support SVCB
queries (returns NODATA or NXDOMAIN for a SVCB query), Discovery
Clients SHOULD fall back to the following mechanism. This section
preserves the Layer 1 from ADP v1.0 (-00) as a backward-compatible
alternative.

section.title: TXT Record

dl.dd: Protocol version. MUST be ADP1, ADP1.0, or ADP1.1.
Public key fingerprint. Computed as SHA-256 of the raw Ed25519

section.t: public key, encoded in base64url without padding.

dl.dd: Full HTTPS URL to the Well-Known agent metadata endpoint.
Application protocol identifier (e.g., a2a).
Service port number. Default: 443.
Agent protocol identifier. Multi-record TXT: Values exceeding

section.t: 255 octets MAY be split across multiple TXT records at the same
owner name. Reassembly concatenates RDATA in returned order.

section.title: SRV Record
section.t: If no SRV record is published, Discovery Clients SHOULD connect to
{domain} on TCP port 443.

section.title: Fallback Procedure
section.t: Query SVCB at {domain}.
If NODATA or NXDOMAIN, proceed to fallback.
Query TXT at _agent.{domain}.
Parse v, pk, wk fields.
Query SRV at _agent._tcp.{domain} to locate host:port.
Proceed to Layer 2 () using the resolved URL and host.
Discovery Clients that successfully use the fallback path SHOULD
indicate this in their user agent or log, as the security properties
of fallback discovery are weaker than SVCB-based discovery (no DANE
support, weaker path validation).

section.title: Caching
section.t: Discovery Clients SHOULD cache Well-Known metadata with respect to the
HTTP Cache-Control headers returned by the server. If no explicit
cache directives are present, clients SHOULD apply a default TTL of
3600 seconds.
Clients MAY use the cap-sha256 SvcParamKey from DNS-AID to detect
changes to the capability descriptor without re-fetching the full
document.

section.title: HTML Landing Page
section.t: The domain root (GET /) MUST return an HTML page suitable for both
human browsing and machine parsing.

section.title: JSON-LD Embedding
section.t: The page MUST embed a <script type="application/ld+json"> block
containing the Agent's full metadata (equivalent to the Well-Known
JSON content).

dl.dt: The page SHOULD include the following meta tags

section.title: Semantic HTML
section.t: Agent landing pages SHOULD use semantic HTML elements and custom
elements (e.g., <agent-card>) to describe capabilities and enable
human interaction. An example landing page structure is provided
in .

section.title: Overview
section.t: AGP is a WebSocket-based messaging protocol that enables real-time
communication between Agents after discovery. It uses JSON as the
message framing format, with Ed25519 signatures for per-message
authentication.

section.title: Connection Handshake

dl.dt: A Discovery Client establishes an AGP connection as follows

section.t: Resolve the Agent's chat endpoint from the Well-Known metadata
(endpoints.chat).
Open a WebSocket connection to the resolved URL using WSS
(WebSocket Secure).
The connecting Agent sends a hello message containing its
Agent URI and public key fingerprint.
The receiving Agent responds with its own hello message.
Both sides verify the counterparty's public key fingerprint
against the value obtained from the Well-Known metadata.
Subsequent messages are signed and verified using Ed25519.

section.title: Message Format
section.t: Each AGP message is a single JSON object with the following

dl.dd: Conversational message between Agents.
Asynchronous task request or result.
Protocol-level control messages (heartbeat, error, disconnect).
Acknowledgment of message receipt.

section.title: Signature Computation
section.t: The signature covers the following fields, concatenated with
The signature is computed using Ed25519 and encoded as
base64url without padding, prefixed with ed25519:.

section.title: Task Endpoint
section.t: The server responds with 202 Accepted and a task status URL.
Results are delivered to the callback endpoint when complete.

section.title: Trust Escalation Model

dl.dt: ADP defines a progressive trust model

dl.dd: The DNS record for the Agent has been resolved. The public key

section.t: fingerprint in the DNS record (SVCB bap or TXT pk) has been
retrieved. No cryptographic verification has been performed.

dl.dd: The TLS endpoint certificate has been validated against the

section.t: DNSSEC-signed TLSA record. The transport channel is
authenticated at the DANE level.

dl.dd: The full Ed25519 public key from the Well-Known metadata has

section.t: been verified to match the fingerprint from the DNS record. The
key is cryptographically bound to the domain.

dl.dd: Bidirectional signature verification has been completed. The

section.t: communication partner's identity is fully authenticated.

section.title: Freshness and Replay Protection
section.t: Each AGP message includes a timestamp. Receivers MUST reject
messages with timestamps more than 300 seconds in the past or more
than 60 seconds in the future (relative to the receiver's clock),
with appropriate clock skew tolerance.
Implementations SHOULD track recently seen message IDs to detect
replay attempts within the validity window.

section.title: Fingerprint Verification
section.t: Discovery Clients MUST verify that the SHA-256 hash of the full
Ed25519 public key obtained from the Well-Known metadata matches the
fingerprint published in the DNS record (SVCB or TXT). If the
fingerprints do not match, the connection MUST be terminated and the
Agent MUST NOT be trusted.

section.title: TLS Requirements
section.t: All endpoints (Well-Known, WebSocket, REST) MUST be served over
TLS 1.3 or later. Certificates MUST be valid and chain to a trusted
root CA. Self-signed certificates are NOT acceptable for production
deployments, except in local development environments.
When TLSA records are published (), Discovery Clients SHOULD
perform DANE verification in addition to standard PKI validation.

dl.dt: Agents that do not wish to be publicly discoverable may

ul.li: Not publish _agent DNS records.
Return HTTP 404 or 403 from the Well-Known endpoint.
Require a bearer token for Well-Known access.
Use invitation-based discovery instead of DNS discovery.

section.title: Well-Known URI Registration
section.t: IANA has denied registration of the "agent" Well-Known URI
in case #1453939 (2026-06). This document therefore
specifies the URI path /.well-known/agent.json as a de facto
convention pending future availability of the Well-Known URI registry
slot. Implementers should be aware that this path has not been
formally registered.

section.title: SvcParamKey Registration (via DNS-AID)
section.t: The SvcParamKeys used by ADP (bap, cap, cap-sha256, well-known) are
registered through the DNS-AID specification
. ADP does not independently
request these registrations.

section.title: Service Name Registration
section.t: ADP uses the service name _agent for SRV records. Formal service
name registration with IANA is pending.

section.title: Backward Compatibility
section.t: ADP v1.1 is backward compatible with ADP v1.0 at the Well-Known
metadata layer. v1.1 adds the dns block and dane auth method to
the schema; v1.0 clients that ignore unknown fields will function
correctly with v1.1 metadata.
The fallback TXT+SRV discovery mechanism () is identical to
the ADP v1.0 Layer 1, ensuring that pre-v1.1 Discovery Clients can
still locate Agents that have migrated to SVCB-based discovery.
